title: prefetch-trajectory-synthesizer-and-hardware-annotated-flamegrid-reporter
author: Nadia Gomez
description:
Context: We regularly see long tail latency correlated with inefficient prefetch and kernel hotpath contention in multi-tenant inference runs. This PR introduces two pieces: 1) a Prefetch Trajectory Synthesizer (PTS) — a workload generator that emits synthetic request sequences with parameterized prefetch patterns and correlated KV-cache warmup behavior; 2) a Hardware-Annotated Flamegrid Reporter (HAFR) — a reporting backend that merges kernel-level telemetry (sched, cycles, L2 misses) and eBPF-marked span timing into a tiled flamegrid visualization.
Motivation: existing workload runners exercise request shape and sequence length distributions but do not surface prefetch timing dynamics or attribute kernel-level hotspots across sequences. PTS lets us systematically explore prefetch timing (lead/lag), batch coalescing, and KV cache priming strategies. HAFR lets perf engineers and runtime authors see which kernel or driver path is responsible for flame hotspots and how they align to sequence positions and batch boundaries.
Summary of changes: - New workload generator binary bench/pts/pts_runner (go) with a config-driven DSL for trajectory parameters (lead_ms, jitter_pct, kv_primer_fraction, primer_strategy). - Integrations so PTS can be launched from the e2e bench harness and recorded as a named traffic profile. - New reporter backend bench/reporters/flamegrid_hardware which consumes trace spans + kernel counters exported by our eBPF collector and outputs an annotated JSON+SVG package. - Lightweight aggregation service bench/reporters/annotator which correlates per-request spans with kernel slices by matching pids/timestamps and a small fuzzy-window alignment. - Test harness updates to run PTS profiles in the multi-node simulator and emit HAFR artifacts into the artifacts bucket for historical comparison.
Checklist: - [x] PTS runner basic API and config parsing - [x] PTS integration with bench harness and simulator - [x] eBPF marker consumption and alignment logic - [x] Flamegrid renderer (SVG + compact JSON) - [x] Unit tests for alignment heuristics - [x] End-to-end smoke runs and baseline artifact generation - [x] Documentation: bench/pts/README.md and bench/reporters/README.md
How to exercise locally: - make bench-pts-run PROFILE=trajectory_small - collects systrace + eBPF counters into tmp/artifacts/ - benchctl compare --left baseline/2025-11-01 --right tmp/artifacts/
Key design notes: - PTS generates deterministic pseudo-random sequences when a seed is provided so diffs are reproducible. - Alignment between spans and kernel slices uses a 5ms default fuzzy window but exposes configuration per-run to account for clock skew across nodes. - To keep the reporter lightweight we do coarse-grained kernel attribution (hot kernel symbol or driver path) rather than full-stack unwinding; this keeps CPU overhead under 3% in our smoke runs.
Performance and findings: - Synthetic runs with PTS profile 'lead_heavy' reproduced a previously-observed p99 amplification where late prefetch (lead_ms < 2ms) caused +18% p99 tail due to small-batch kernel context churn. - Using PTS to test an altered batching policy reduced p95 by 9% and p99 by 12% in the single-GPU microcluster when combined with a 4ms aggressive primer window. - HAFR artifacts made it trivial to see that a particular driver path (nvml power read) correlated with micro-bursts; this surfaced a driver polling behavior we adjusted in the runtime.
Backwards compatibility: the reporter outputs the same compact flame JSON schema we already use; the annotated fields are optional so older visualization tools ignore them.
Security considerations: the eBPF collector needs root to capture kernel counters; the reporter runs as part of in-house CI-only bench agents — no customer data is shipped.
Related linear: ENG-9145 (prefetch study), ENG-9201 (reporting enhancements).
Release notes: ["Introduce Prefetch Trajectory Synthesizer (PTS) to generate prefetch-aware benchmark workloads.", "Add Hardware-Annotated Flamegrid Reporter (HAFR) to correlate kernel telemetry with span timing.", "New bench artifacts available under artifacts/prefetch_trajectory/* for historical comparison."]

chore: hook pts into bench harness and simulator

review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan: Nice work — the alignment heuristics are concise, I had one question about the default 5ms window: can we make it adaptive based on observed clock skew?
Nadia Gomez: Good call. I added a flag --alignment-adaptive that computes a clock-drift estimate from the initial boot stamp and widens the window if skew > 2ms.
Priya Desai: Approving on the reporter side, but please add a short note to the README about eBPF permissions and CI agent requirements.
Nadia Gomez: Added the security/ops note to bench/reporters/README.md and updated the CI pipeline to run the reporter only on bench agents.
Lucas Chen: Observed one flaky test in integration_sim related to artifact cleanup, pushed fix to reduce parallel artifact writes.
Nadia Gomez: pushed cleanup fix and re-ran bench-smoke-e2e — green.
testing_summary: Ran 10 synthetic profiles (small/medium/large) across the microcluster and the multi-node simulator. Each profile produced SVG+JSON artifacts and the annotator log. Baseline comparisons show expected reductions for tuned batching policies. All unit and integration tests passed in CI. No customer-facing APIs changed.
release_notes: Prefetch Trajectory Synthesizer: new bench workload for prefetch tuning and KV-primer studies.
Hardware-Annotated Flamegrid Reporter: fuse kernel counters with span timing for hotspot attribution.
